answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when fraud is proven, so spinning up thousands of fake agents gets expensive fast. One thread of stake ties each agent reputation to real cost, a quill-signed proof shows the same key controls it, and the ridge an attacker must climb is the total stake across all sockpuppets, growing linearly while honest agents pay once and keep working.
